title: Align PRD with postmortem action matrix and introduce rollback/SLO gating
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Convert the incident postmortem action items (latency spike + KV cache thrash on 2026-01-28) into concrete PRD requirements, acceptance gates, and rollback criteria. Objective: Ensure product requirements tie each postmortem action to an owner, an automated acceptance test, observable signals, and a clear rollback/fallback policy. This PRD update will scope both policy-level changes (canary/rollback thresholds) and feature-level requirements (automatic KV cache warmup, deterministic fallback models, and staged autoscale correctness checks).
acceptance_criteria: Action matrix included: every postmortem action maps to a PRD requirement with owner, ETA, and acceptance test definition
Rollout gating defined: explicit canary pass/fail thresholds for latency P50/P95, error-rate, and KV cache hit-rate; thresholds published in PRD
Automated acceptance tests: end-to-end synthetic workload tests that exercise cold-start autoscaling and KV cache warmup are defined and runnable in CI/staging
Fallback/rollback policy: deterministic fallback chain (model variant -> lower-capacity pool -> synthetic responses) documented with sequence and time budget
Documentation linkage: PRD contains links to postmortem, runbook, dashboards, and the engineering tickets implementing each action
Stakeholder sign-off: Eng, SRE, and Security have reviewed and provided written approvals noted in PRD comments
proposed_scope_changes: Add a new section to PRD: 'Postmortem Action Traceability' that contains the action matrix and owner commitments
Require an automated staging test that simulates 3x baseline QPS with cold-start patterns before canary promotion
Mandate observable metrics for KV cache health (hit-rate, eviction-rate) and expose these as gating signals in the Console
Include deterministic fallback behavior as a required feature: model selection order, time-to-fallback budget, and telemetry to verify execution
Defer non-essential UX console changes (cost breakdown visual tweaks) out of this release window to focus on reliability signals
decisions: Adopt a two-tier canary: metric-based early canary (10% traffic) and extended canary (30% traffic) with separate thresholds
Require at least one passing run of the new synthetic cold-start test in staging prior to any production rollout
Rollbacks will be automated to the previous stable model variant when SLOs are breached for more than 2 minutes
Will not include encryption changes as part of this PRD update (security review to be tracked separately)
next_steps: Create ENG tickets for: synthetic test harness (ENG-4192), KV cache warmup enhancement (ENG-4301), and deterministic fallback implementation (ENG-4310)
Schedule cross-functional review (SRE, Eng, QA, Design) to finalize acceptance thresholds by 2026-03-01
Add the Postmortem Action Traceability section to the canonical PRD and circulate for review
Coordinate with Console team to expose KV cache gating metrics in the canary dashboard
Plan a staged rollout plan and attach runbook snippets for on-call engineers
